summary: Clofazimine (Lamprene) is a riminophenazine antimycobacterial used primarily for leprosy, including erythema nodosum leprosum reactions, and as a component of drug-resistant tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacterial regimens. It causes a characteristic reddish-brown to black skin and conjunctival discoloration and accumulates extensively in tissues with a very long half-life. The most important risks are dose- and duration-dependent GI effects (including rare crystal deposition enteropathy/bowel obstruction) and QT prolongation. In the US it is supplied through a restricted/IND or orphan program rather than routine commercial distribution.

Treatment of nontuberculous mycobacterial infections, e.g., Mycobacterium avium complex (off-label)

moa: Binds preferentially to mycobacterial DNA (guanine-rich sequences), inhibiting growth; also generates reactive oxygen species and has membrane-destabilizing and anti-inflammatory actions, the latter underlying its benefit in erythema nodosum leprosum.

relative: QT prolongation or use with other QT-prolonging drugs

preg: Crosses the placenta and may discolor the neonate's skin; use only if the benefit justifies the potential risk. Reserve for clear indications.
lact: Excreted in breast milk and may cause skin pigmentation in the breastfed infant; weigh benefit against risk.
renal: No specific dose adjustment; eliminated slowly, mainly via feces with extensive tissue storage.
hepatic: Use with caution and monitor liver function; rare hepatotoxicity reported.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., bedaquiline, fluoroquinolones, antiarrhythmics) - additive QT prolongation
moderate: Rifampicin - may modestly reduce clofazimine absorption rate
Other GI-toxic agents - additive GI effects
minor: Dapsone - possible reduced anti-inflammatory effect of clofazimine (variable reports)
interactions.food: Take with food/milk to enhance absorption
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG (QT) when combined with other QT-prolonging agents (notably bedaquiline).

pearls: Source: US Lamprene prescribing information, WHO leprosy/TB guidance, and BNF; this label was not retrievable via openFDA at time of authoring (orphan/restricted distribution)
Characteristic reddish-brown skin and conjunctival discoloration - counsel before starting; reversible over months to years
Extremely long half-life (~70 days) from massive tissue/fat accumulation
High-dose or prolonged use can cause clofazimine crystal enteropathy and bowel obstruction - keep high doses short
Both antimycobacterial and anti-inflammatory - useful for erythema nodosum leprosum; watch QT with bedaquiline
missed: Take the missed daily dose with food when remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. For supervised monthly doses, take as directed by the program. Do not double doses.
overdose: Limited data; expected effects are severe GI symptoms and accentuated pigmentation. There is no specific antidote. Provide supportive and symptomatic care, including management of GI complications; the very long half-life means effects resolve slowly.
